q: Sec. 32.02 deals with Owner insurance against contingent liability for injury or death arising from the Contract's operations. How does it treat that coverage?
o: Required only when the Contractor carries no liability insurance
Optional — the Owner may carry it if he chooses
Not allowed, since it would duplicate the Contractor's policy
n: Sec. 32.02 (Owner's Optional Insurance) makes this coverage optional, at the Owner's election. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 32, Sec. 32.02)

q: Sec. 22.02 limits how often the Contractor may file a Request for Payment for work done. What is that limit?
o: No more often than once a month
n: Sec. 22.02 (Requests for Payment) allows the Contractor to submit a Request for Payment periodically but not more than once a month. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.02)

q: Complete the statement based on the closing clause of Art. 15 (the provision numbered 15.01 that follows 15.11): the Contractor must take down all temporary work it put up and clean the premises as a condition for ___.
o: completion of the work and the Owner's acceptance of it
issuance of the Notice to Proceed
return of the Contractor's Proposal Bond
approval of the Schedule of Completion
n: The closing clause of Art. 15 (Removal of Temporary Structures) requires the Contractor to remove all temporary work and clean the premises as a condition for completing the work and before the Owner's acceptance. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 15 (Removal of Temporary Structures))

q: Sec. 2.03(c) places responsibility for the adequacy of the design and the sufficiency of the Drawings and Specifications on which party?
n: Sec. 2.03(c) places responsibility for adequacy of design and sufficiency of Drawings/Specifications on the Owner (through the Architect/Engineer as representative). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 2, Sec. 2.03(c))

q: Per Sec. 33.04(d), the parties have laid out their evidence but the Architect has not decided. After how many days without a decision may either party call for arbitration?
n: Sec. 33.04(d) allows either party to demand arbitration if the Architect fails to render a decision within fifteen (15) days after the parties have presented their evidence. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.04(d))

q: An approved Request for Payment is not paid by the Owner on time. What does Sec. 22.07 impose on the unpaid amount?
o: Interest at bank lending rates at signing
n: Sec. 22.07 provides that the Owner's failure to pay is subject to interest based on prevailing banking loan rates at the time the Contract was signed. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.07)

q: Art. 18 covers emergencies that threaten life, the work, or neighboring property. What does it allow the Contractor to do?
o: Wait for written authority from the Architect or Owner before doing anything
Stop all work and clear the site until the Owner inspects
Use his own judgment, without special instruction or authority, to prevent the threatened loss or injury
Refer the matter to the Board of Arbitration first
n: Art. 18 (Sec. 18.01) authorizes the Contractor to act at his discretion in an emergency, without waiting for special instructions, to prevent loss or injury. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 18, Sec. 18.01)

q: While preparing its bid, a Contractor spots what looks like a conflict between two Specifications sections, but it submits its proposal without asking the Architect for a written ruling. After award, it uses the cheaper of the two methods. What follows under Sec. 3.03(a)?
o: The Owner pays for the extra cost
He is presumed to have priced the costlier one
He may pick either method freely
n: Sec. 3.03(a): absent a pre-bid written decision from the Architect, the Contractor is deemed to have estimated the more expensive way of doing the work; if the less expensive method is used after award, the Contractor must credit the Owner the difference. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 3, Sec. 3.03(a))

q: Art. 34(c) describes the Architect's stance when interpreting the Contract and judging how it is performed. Which best characterizes it?
o: He favors the Owner who engaged him
He defers to the Project Representative
n: Art. 34(c) requires the Architect, as interpreter of the Contract and judge of its performance, to side with neither party but to enforce faithful performance by both. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 34(c))

q: Even after final payment, Sec. 22.13(a) keeps the Contractor liable to fix defects from faulty materials or workmanship (and pay for resulting damage) if they show up within how long after the Owner accepts the work?
n: Sec. 22.13(a) (Correction of Work After Final Payment) fixes this liability period at one year from the date of acceptance of the work by the Owner. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.13(a))

q: The Architect has covered work opened up because it may not conform, but it proves to meet the Contract. Apart from a suitable time extension, what does Sec. 20.03(d) pay the Contractor for the labor and materials spent on the examination and replacement?
o: Actual cost only, with no markup
Nothing, since re-examination is a normal risk of the trade
n: Sec. 20.03(d) provides that if examined work is found to meet Contract requirements, the actual cost of labor and materials plus 15 percent shall be allowed the Contractor, along with a time extension if completion was delayed. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.03(d))

q: Sec. 5.05 sets how many prints of shop drawings go to the Architect for approval and how disapproved drawings are resubmitted. Which is correct?
o: Two sets at first; resubmit in triplicate
One set at first; resubmit a single original
Three sets at first; resubmit in duplicate until approved
Four sets at first; resubmit in duplicate
n: Sec. 5.05 requires three sets of prints of shop drawings for approval; Sec. 5.05(a) requires corrected shop drawings to be resubmitted in duplicate until the Architect's approval is obtained. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 5, Sec. 5.05)

q: How do the General Conditions describe Section XI, the Schedule of Time Limits?
o: A section for government projects only
An index of all time limits in one place
An annex that overrides the Articles
n: The introduction to Section XI states it is an indexed section, based on the entire General Conditions, provided to facilitate execution of the Contractor's work by consolidating time limits from the various Articles. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Section XI (Schedule of Time Limits), introductory note)

q: A Contractor's work relies on the proper work of a separate contractor, but the Contractor does not inspect that work and report its defects. Under Sec. 24.03, this failure:
o: Makes the Owner liable for defects
Acceptance of that work, except later defects
n: Sec. 24.03 provides that failure to inspect and report defects in a separate contractor's work is deemed an acceptance of that work as fit for the Contractor's own subsequent work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 24, Sec. 24.03)

q: Per Sec. 20.07(a), how must Owner-ordered changes that alter, add to, or deduct from the work be made?
o: In writing, signed by the Owner
n: Sec. 20.07(a) requires Owner-ordered changes to be in writing; no change/omission is considered authorized without the Owner's signed written instructions. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.07(a))

q: Sec. 7.01 assigns the job of obtaining and paying for the construction permits and licenses the work needs. Who generally handles this?
o: The Contractor, unless the Contract says otherwise
n: Sec. 7.01 places the duty of securing permits/licenses and paying required fees on the Contractor, with possible Owner reimbursement only if stipulated in prior instructions. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 7, Sec. 7.01)

q: UAP Doc. 301 lists five Contract Documents: the Agreement, the General Conditions, the Special Provisions, the Specifications, and one more. Which is the missing item?
n: Sec. 1.01 enumerates the Contract Documents as: (a) Agreement, (b) General Conditions, (c) Special Provisions, (d) Specifications, (e) Drawings. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.01)

q: In a dispute between the Contractor and a Sub-contractor, must the Architect decide first before the matter can go to arbitration, per Sec. 26.03?
o: Only when the Owner is a party
No — it is not a condition precedent
n: Sec. 26.03 provides that between the Contractor and Sub-contractor, an Architect's decision need not be a condition precedent to arbitration, unlike the general rule for Owner-Contractor disputes. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 26, Sec. 26.03)

q: Owner-caused delay (such as late Owner-supplied materials) is affecting the Contractor. Under Sec. 20.08, the Contractor keeps a valid claim for extra cost only if written notice is given within how many days of recognizing the delay?
n: Sec. 20.08 requires written notice within fifteen days after recognition of a delay attributable to the Owner, or no claim shall be valid. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.08)

q: Laws, ordinances, regulations, or building codes are revised while construction is underway, and the change affects the Contract's cost or completion time. What does Art. 8 (General, Equipment and Materials) provide?
o: The Contractor carries the extra cost without adjustment
The Owner may end the Contract at once
The work is suspended until the Architect rules
n: Art. 8 provides that where a legal revision made during construction affects cost or time, a corresponding adjustment shall be made to the Contract. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 8)

q: A construction firm is bidding on a project under UAP 301. Per Sec. 1.11 and 1.12, how large must the Performance Bond and the Payment Bond each be, and when are they posted?
o: 15% of the Contract amount each, before the Contract is executed
10% each, within 7 days after the Notice to Proceed
30% each, before the Contract is executed
15% each, upon issuance of the Certificate of Completion
n: Secs. 1.11-1.12 (confirmed at Sec. 31.03) require a Performance Bond and a Payment Bond each equal to 15% of the Contract amount, furnished before execution of the Contract. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Secs. 1.11-1.12; Art. 31, Sec. 31.03)

q: Once the Contract is terminated and the work taken over, what damages may be recovered from the original Contractor and/or his sureties under Sec. 29.04?
o: Liquidated damages plus excess completion cost
n: Sec. 29.04 entitles the Owner to recover both (a) accrued daily liquidated damages up to takeover and (b) the excess cost of completing the project over the Contract Price, including added professional/administrative costs. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 29, Sec. 29.04)

q: Unless the Contract says otherwise, Sec. 21.02 starts counting Contract Time on which day after the Notice to Proceed (NTP) is received?
n: Sec. 21.02 provides that computation of Contract Time commences on the seventh (7th) day from receipt of the Notice to Proceed, unless otherwise stipulated, with every calendar day thereafter counted as a working day. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.02)

q: A material, article, or process is specified only by trade name. Under Sec. 10.03(b), a substitute may be used:
o: whenever it costs less than the specified item
only with the Owner's verbal consent
only with the Architect's written approval
n: Sec. 10.03(b) allows substitution of a specified trade-name material only with the Architect's written approval. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 10, Sec. 10.03(b))

q:
Consider these two UAP Doc. 301 definitions:
(1) General Conditions — printed documents that set out the procedural and administrative aspects of the contract.
(2) Special Provisions — instructions issued before bidding to add to or modify the Drawings, Specifications and/or General Conditions.
Which statement is true?
n: Sec. 1.19 defines General Conditions and Sec. 1.20 defines Special Provisions exactly as stated in both (1) and (2). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Secs. 1.19-1.20)

q: Under Sec. 31.01, the Contractor's liability insurance policy must include a clause that bars the insurer from cancelling it without giving the Owner how many days' written notice of intent to cancel?
n: Sec. 31.01 requires the liability insurance policy to provide that it will not be cancelled without ten (10) days' written notice to the Owner. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.01)

q: The Contractor wants to pause the work for a while (not because of an accident) to move equipment elsewhere. How much advance written notice to the Architect does Sec. 21.04(f) require before the work is suspended?
n: Sec. 21.04(f) requires the Contractor to give the Architect written notice at least ten (10) days prior to beginning, suspending (except in case of accident), or resuming work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.04(f))
scenario: Under a UAP Doc. 301 building contract, the Contractor is handed a Notice to Proceed (NTP) dated March 1. From that date, the Contractor must keep track of several contract-administration deadlines set by Art. 21 (Time of Completion).

q: Under Art. 11, what does the mere fact that the Owner supplies certain materials establish about them?
o: It is conclusive evidence that they are acceptable for their intended purpose
They become the Contractor's property on delivery
They must pass additional testing before use
The Contractor must warrant them as if they were his own materials
n: Art. 11 provides that the Owner furnishing the material is conclusive evidence of its acceptability for the intended purpose, and the Contractor may continue to use it until otherwise directed. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 11)

q: A brief, very light drizzle causes a small, easily fixed delay on site. May the Contractor claim reparation for damages under Sec. 1.26 (Act of God or Force Majeure)?
o: No — trivial weather is not force majeure
Yes — if rain lasts over an hour
n: Sec. 1.26 expressly excludes natural phenomena of inconsequential degree for the locality from the definition of Act of God/Force Majeure, so no reparation is made to the Contractor for resulting damage. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.26)

q: During the guarantee period, the Contractor receives written notice of defective work. How many days does Sec. 31.05(d) give him to make the repairs at his own cost?
n: Sec. 31.05(d) requires the Contractor to complete repairs and corrective work within five (5) days after written notice from the Owner, at his own cost. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.05(d))

q: Sec. 22.01 requires the Contractor to submit its Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value within how many days of receiving the Notice to Proceed?
n: Sec. 22.01 requires the Contractor to submit the complete Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the Notice to Proceed. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.01)

q: The Contractor's temporary office under Sec. 15.01 must include a room for the Architect's use. About how large must that room be?
n: Sec. 15.01 (Temporary Office and Contractor's Building) requires one room of approximately 12 square meters to be provided for the Architect's use. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 15, Sec. 15.01)

q: Under Art. 2, in how many copies must the Owner and the Contractor sign the Contract Documents, with witnesses?
n: Sec. 2.01 requires the Contract Documents to be signed in quintuplicate (five copies) by the Owner and Contractor, duly witnessed. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 2, Sec. 2.01)

q: Before final payment or any part of the retention falls due, a sub-contractor refuses to give a lien release or receipt in full. What alternative does Sec. 33.01 (Liens) give the Contractor?
o: Ask the Owner to file suit against the sub-contractor
Post a bond acceptable to the Owner that protects him against any lien
Deposit the disputed amount with the Architect
n: Sec. 33.01 allows the Contractor to furnish an indemnity bond satisfactory to the Owner in lieu of a lien release/receipt when a sub-contractor refuses to furnish one. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.01)

q: Under Sec. 22.03(a), which set of requirements applies to the progress photographs that go with each Request for Payment?
n: Sec. 22.03(a) requires 6"x8" photographs, four exposures (one on each side of the building) per period, and eight prints (2 copies of each exposure) delivered to the Architect. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.03(a))

q: From the start of operations until the building is fully finished, Sec. 16.01(a) requires the Contractor to guard the site with:
o: A security agency hired by the Owner
No guard if the site is fenced
n: Sec. 16.01(a) requires the Contractor to provide reliable and competent watchmen to guard the site from commencement until full completion. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 16, Sec. 16.01(a))

q: At the end of the work and before Final Payment, what does Sec. 2.05 require the Contractor to do with the Drawings, Specifications, and Models the Architect provided?
o: Return them, except the contract set
n: Sec. 2.05 states the Drawings, Specifications, and Models (with additional instructions) are the property of the Architect and, except the signed contract set, must be returned to the Architect before Final Payment. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 2, Sec. 2.05)

q: How is a formal Board of Arbitration formed under Sec. 33.05(b), and what vote decides its rulings?
o: One named by the Owner; unanimous
Three named by the Architect; unanimous
One each from Owner and Contractor, plus a chair; majority
n: Sec. 33.05(b) describes a three-member Board (one appointed by each party, plus a jointly-appointed chairman), with decisions requiring only a simple majority. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.05(b))

q: The Contractor's billings now stand at 68% of the Contract Price. Because this is above 65%, what must it submit under Sec. 22.09 before any further payment on the excess can be made?
o: A sworn statement that bills are paid
n: Sec. 22.09 (Payments Over 65 Percent) requires a sworn statement that all labor and material bills have been duly paid, except bills specifically enumerated as unpaid, before payment on contracts exceeding 65% of the Contract Price. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.09)
scenario: Under a building contract governed by UAP Doc. 301, the Contractor's total billings to date have just gone past 65% of the Contract Price, which activates the special payment safeguard of Sec. 22.09.

q: When the Contractor supervises the work in person instead of employing an engineer or architect to do it, what does Sec. 19.02 require of him?
o: He must be a licensed engineer or architect
He must be a civil engineer with at least 10 years of experience
He must be approved by the local government
n: Sec. 19.02 requires that if the Contractor personally supervises the work, he must be a licensed engineer or architect; otherwise he must employ one acceptable to the Architect, who must inspect the site at least once a week. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 19, Sec. 19.02)

q: A discrepancy in figures or drawings is found during construction. What does Sec. 3.04 require?
o: Report it to the Architect before adjusting
Ignore it if under 5% of the work
n: Sec. 3.04 (Discrepancies in Drawings) requires immediate submission to the Architect before any adjustment, or the Contractor bears the risk and expense. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 3, Sec. 3.04)

q: Under Art. 35(a), responsibility for the Engineers' own designs, computations, and professional services in preparing the Drawings and Specifications rests solely with:
n: Art. 35(a) makes the Engineers solely responsible for their own respective designs, computations, and professional services. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 35(a))

q: Sec. 22.14 (Release of Retention) says the Owner releases the retained amount how long after the date of final payment?
n: Sec. 22.14 requires the retention amount to be released within three months after the date of final payment. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.14)

q: On this contract, actual excavation quantities came out higher than those in the Proposal. Under Sec. 20.06, what percentage of overrun or underrun from Proposal quantities is considered a normal margin that does NOT call for a change in the Contract Price?
n: Sec. 20.06 (Increased or Decreased Quantities of Work) treats overruns/underruns up to five percent (5%) of Proposal quantities as a normal margin of adjustment not changing the Contract Price. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.06)
scenario: A Php 20,000,000 lump-sum building contract under UAP Doc. 301 is in progress. Over the course of construction, a number of quantity and cost adjustments come up, and each is being checked against the General Conditions' rules on changes, extra work, and time extensions.

q: Per Sec. 5.04, shop drawings must be sent with a letter of transmittal in what form?
o: None — no transmittal letter is needed
n: Sec. 5.04 requires shop drawing submissions to be accompanied by a letter of transmittal in duplicate. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 5, Sec. 5.04)

q: The Owner and the Contractor cannot settle a factual dispute. Both have presented their evidence, but the Architect has not decided. Reading Sec. 33.04(d) together with Item 8 of the Schedule of Time Limits, after how many days without a decision may either party demand arbitration?
n: Both Sec. 33.04(d) and Item 8 of the Schedule of Time Limits confirm that either party may demand arbitration if the Architect fails to decide within fifteen (15) days after the parties present their evidence. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Section XI, Item 8; Art. 33, Sec. 33.04(d))

q: Does Sec. 25.01 allow the Contractor to sublet or sub-contract the WHOLE of the work under the Contract?
o: No — only parts may be sublet
n: Sec. 25.01 prohibits subletting/sub-contracting the ENTIRE work, while allowing any part or specialty work to be sublet subject to the competency-evaluation provisions of Sec. 25.02. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 25, Sec. 25.01)

q: Sec. 20.07(f) lets the Architect, rather than the Owner, order which kind of changes directly through his instructions?
o: Only changes that lower the price
Minor, no-cost changes that fit the design
n: Sec. 20.07(f) (Changes Ordered by the Architect) limits the Architect's unilateral authority to minor changes not involving extra cost and consistent with the design concept. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.07(f))

q: Unless the task is passed to the Contractor at the Owner's cost, who is responsible under Sec. 7.03 for having a certified surveyor establish lot lines, boundary lines, easements, and benchmarks?
n: Sec. 7.03 (Construction Stakes and Reference Marks) makes the Owner responsible for establishing lot lines, boundary lines, easements, and benchmarks via a certified surveyor, unless relegated to the Contractor at the Owner's cost. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 7, Sec. 7.03)

q: Which party does UAP Doc. 301 define as the one who orders the project to be carried out, including its duly appointed successors or authorized representatives?
n: Sec. 1.02 defines the Owner as the person or entity ordering the project for execution, including successors or authorized representatives. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.02)

q: A court or public authority orders the Contractor's work stopped entirely for 95 straight days, through no fault of the Contractor. Under Sec. 27(a), does this give the Contractor the right to suspend or terminate the Contract?
o: Yes — but only after a year
Yes — over 90 days is a ground to suspend
n: Art. 27(a) allows the Contractor to suspend or terminate (upon 15 days' written notice) if a court or public authority order stops the work for 90 days through no fault of the Contractor; 95 days satisfies this. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 27(a))
scenario: Under a UAP Doc. 301 contract, a Contractor is reviewing whether recent events on its project give it grounds, under Art. 27, to suspend the work or terminate the Contract, each option carrying its own required written notice period.

q: The work completed on a building project is valued at 96% of the contract amount, and only minor items are left. Has "Substantial Completion" been reached under Sec. 20.11?
n: Sec. 20.11 defines Substantial Completion as the value of work completed being not less than 98% of the contract amount and the remaining unfinished work being minor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.11)

q: What is the purpose, under Sec. 9.01, of naming certain equipment in the Specifications by brand name and catalogue number?
o: To set a standard of quality, while still letting other products of equal or better quality and fully suitable design compete
To rule out every other manufacturer
To lock the Contractor into that brand with no substitution allowed
To let the Owner approve equipment without the Architect or Engineer
n: Sec. 9.01 clarifies that naming equipment by brand/catalogue number establishes quality standards but does not eliminate other suitable products from competition, subject to substitution procedures. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 9, Sec. 9.01)

q: The Owner has just released a Contractor's 15% Performance Bond and 15% Payment Bond. What bond must the Contractor put up next under the General Conditions, and at what percentage of the Contract Price?
n: Sec. 1.13 (and Sec. 31.04) defines the Guaranteed Bond, furnished at 30% of the Total Contract Cost, given only after the Performance and Payment Bonds are released, to guarantee quality of materials and workmanship. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.13; Art. 31, Sec. 31.04)

q: After the Contract is terminated, can the Contractor recover prospective profits on work done after termination, per Sec. 29.03(b)?
o: Yes, at the original contract rate
Yes, up to 10% of the unfinished work
No — no claim for prospective profits on work done after termination is considered or allowed
Only if the Owner finishes the work using the Contractor's former Sub-contractors
n: Sec. 29.03(b) bars any claim for prospective profits on work performed after the Contract's termination. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 29, Sec. 29.03(b))

q: With the Notice to Proceed received on March 1 and no other stipulation, on what date does Contract Time start to run under Sec. 21.02?
o: March 1, the day it was received
n: Since Contract Time computation commences on the 7th day from receipt of NTP, counting from March 1, the 7th day is March 8. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.02)
scenario: Under a UAP Doc. 301 building contract, the Contractor is handed a Notice to Proceed (NTP) dated March 1. From that date, the Contractor must keep track of several contract-administration deadlines set by Art. 21 (Time of Completion).

q: Sec. 10.04 assigns the cost of shipping, delivering, handling, and testing material samples to:
n: Sec. 10.04 (Testing Samples of Materials) places all costs for shipment, delivery, handling, and testing of samples on the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 10, Sec. 10.04)

q: In the General Conditions, which document is the written or printed description of the work to be done, stating the quality of materials and the method of construction?
o: Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value
n: Sec. 1.21 defines Specifications in exactly these terms, distinct from Drawings (graphical presentations, Sec. 1.18). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.21)

q: The Contractor is preparing its Performance Bond and Payment Bond under Sec. 31.03 before signing the Contract. How much must EACH bond be worth?
n: Sec. 31.03 requires a Performance Bond equal to 15% of the Contract amount and a separate 15% Payment Bond: 15% of Php 8,000,000 = Php 1,200,000 each. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.03)
scenario: A Php 8,000,000 building contract under UAP Doc. 301 has been awarded to a Contractor. Before the Contract is signed, the Contractor must post the bonds that Art. 31 requires, and it must later replace those bonds in the order that Article sets out.

q: Under Sec. 21.04(b), what must be attached to the Contractor's request for a time extension before it goes to the Owner for consideration?
o: The written consent of the Bondsmen
Proof that all sub-contractors have been paid
n: Sec. 21.04(b) requires the written consent of the bondsmen to be attached to any Contractor request for extension of time. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.04(b))

q: Under Art. 12 (Royalties and Patents), who pays royalties and license fees for patented materials and processes the Contractor supplies, and who defends any infringement suits?
n: Art. 12 requires the Contractor to pay all royalties and license fees on patented materials/processes he furnishes, defend related suits, and hold the Owner harmless. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 12)

q: Among these Art. 1 definitions, which one is paired WRONGLY?
o: "Furnish" — to purchase and/or fabricate and deliver to the jobsite
"Install" — to build in, mount in position, connect, or apply a specified object so it is ready for use
"Provide" — only to deliver materials to the jobsite without installing them
n: Secs. 1.30-1.32 define Furnish, Install, and Provide (= furnish AND install); choice (d) misstates Provide, which by definition includes installation, not delivery alone. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Secs. 1.30-1.32)

q: If no longer period is specified, how long does the Contractor's guaranty on materials and workmanship last under Sec. 31.05(c), counted from the date of the final certificate?
n: Sec. 31.05(c) sets the default guaranty/warranty period at one year (or longer if the Specifications provide), from the date of the final certificate issued by the Architect. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.05(c))

q: A Request for Payment for Php 3,000,000 of work done is filed under Sec. 22.02 while the Contract is only 30% complete overall. With no other agreement, what retention applies?
n: Sec. 22.02 provides that each Request for Payment is computed less a 10% retention (unless otherwise agreed), until 50% of the Contract has been accomplished. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.02)
scenario: Progress payments are being billed on a Php 10,000,000 building contract governed by UAP Doc. 301. For any given billing, the Contract's cumulative percentage of completion at that time decides which retention rules and payment procedures apply.

q: Under Sec. 15.06, how many painted project signs (naming the Architect, Contractor, and sub-contractors) may the Contractor put up, and who approves their size, color, lettering, and location?
o: Two signs, approved by the Owner
One sign, approved by the Architect
As many as he wants, with no approval needed
One sign, approved by the local building official
n: Sec. 15.06 (Temporary Signs) allows the Contractor to erect one painted sign as approved by the Architect, who approves its size, color, lettering, and location. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 15, Sec. 15.06)

q: On one detail the Drawings and Specifications disagree; on another point the General Conditions disagree with the detailed specifications. How does Sec. 2.03(a) settle these?
o: Specs over drawings; details over General Conditions
n: Sec. 2.03(a): where Drawings and Specifications vary, Specifications control; where General Conditions conflict with detailed specifications requirements, the detailed specifications control. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 2, Sec. 2.03(a))

q: May the Contractor assign the Contract, wholly or partly, or sublet any part of the work without consent, under Sec. 33.02(a)?
o: Yes, if the Architect is told later
No — written Owner consent is needed
n: Sec. 33.02(a) requires the Owner's prior written consent for assignment or subletting, and even with consent the Contractor remains fully responsible and liable for the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.02(a))

q: After receiving a Request for Payment, how many days does the Architect have under Sec. 22.04 to either issue a Certificate of Payment or withhold the Request?
n: Sec. 22.04 requires the Architect to act (issue a Certificate of Payment or withhold it, with written reasons) within fifteen (15) days after receipt of a Request for Payment. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.04)

q: Under Sec. 16.03(a), the Contractor transplants trees and plants at his own expense when they stand within what distance of the building lines?
n: Sec. 16.03(a) requires the Contractor, at his own expense, to transplant trees and plants that need to be relocated within fifty (50) meters from the building lines. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 16, Sec. 16.03(a))

q: Sec. 3.01 requires the Owner to give the Contractor, free of charge, how many sets of Drawings and Specifications?
n: Sec. 3.01 requires the Owner to furnish the Contractor three sets of Drawings and Specifications free of charge; additional copies are at the Contractor's cost of reproduction. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 3, Sec. 3.01)

q: Under Sec. 33.05(c), must there be a decision of the arbitrators before either party may take legal action against the other?
o: No — court is open at any time
Yes — it is a condition precedent
Only for claims over Php 1 million
n: Sec. 33.05(c) makes the arbitrators' decision a condition precedent to either party's right of legal action against the other. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.05(c))

q: The Owner removes condemned work, and the Contractor does not pay for the removal within ten days. After another ten days' written notice, what may the Owner do under Sec. 22.10?
o: Sell them and account for the net proceeds
n: Sec. 22.10 allows the Owner, upon the Contractor's failure to pay removal expenses within 10 days, to sell the condemned materials at auction or private sale (after a further 10 days' written notice) and account for net proceeds. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.10)

q: When the Contractor employs a supervising engineer instead of supervising in person, how often at minimum must that engineer inspect the site under Sec. 19.02?
n: Sec. 19.02 requires the licensed engineer or architect acceptable to the Architect to supervise the work personally and inspect at least once a week. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 19, Sec. 19.02)

q: What contractual weight do additional detail drawings and instructions issued by the Architect during construction carry under Sec. 4.01?
o: The same force as those that originally came with the specifications
They rank below the original specifications
They bind only if the Owner signs them personally
n: Sec. 4.01 states such additional drawings/instructions are considered of equal force as those originally accompanying the specifications. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 4, Sec. 4.01)

q: Under Sec. 36.03, if a Project Representative, Resident Engineer, or Construction Inspector disagrees with the Contractor over materials or the work, what may that on-site representative do?
o: Change the Contract Price without the Architect's approval
Reject the materials or suspend the work until the matter is referred to and decided by the Architect
Terminate the Contract on his own
Nothing — only the Architect may act, and the representative has no interim authority
n: Sec. 36.03 grants Project Representatives/Resident Engineers/Construction Inspectors authority to reject materials or suspend work pending the Architect's decision on the disputed issue. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 36, Sec. 36.03)

q: In one billing period the Contractor completes Php 2,500,000 of work while the contract is still under the 50% completion mark. A 10% retention applies and there is no earlier unpaid balance on that item. To the nearest peso, what net amount (before other deductions) will the Architect certify?
n: Per Sec. 22.02, a 10% retention is deducted: Php 2,500,000 x (1 - 0.10) = Php 2,250,000 net of retention. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.02)
scenario: Progress payments are being billed on a Php 10,000,000 building contract governed by UAP Doc. 301. For any given billing, the Contract's cumulative percentage of completion at that time decides which retention rules and payment procedures apply.

q: The Owner orders extra work on this contract, priced on actual direct cost. Under Sec. 20.07(d)(3), what percentage is added to that direct cost to cover the Contractor's profit, overhead, and contractor's tax?
n: Sec. 20.07(d)(3) allows actual direct cost PLUS Fifteen Percent (15%) for the Contractor's profit, overhead, and contractor's tax as one method of valuing extra work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.07(d)(3))
scenario: A Php 20,000,000 lump-sum building contract under UAP Doc. 301 is in progress. Over the course of construction, a number of quantity and cost adjustments come up, and each is being checked against the General Conditions' rules on changes, extra work, and time extensions.

q: The Architect gives "general" approval to a Contractor's shop drawings. Does Sec. 5.06 treat that approval as relieving the Contractor of responsibility for their accuracy?
o: No, unless deviations were flagged and approved
No — unless the Owner also signs
n: Sec. 5.06 (Responsibility for Accuracy) makes clear that general approval of shop drawings does not relieve the Contractor of responsibility for accuracy or deviations unless specifically flagged in writing and approved. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 5, Sec. 5.06)

q: Taken as a whole, the eleven Sections of UAP Doc. 301 mainly govern the relationships and the procedural and administrative rules among which parties?
n: Across its eleven Sections, UAP Doc. 301's General Conditions govern the procedural and administrative relationship principally among the Owner, the Architect, and the Contractor, with Engineers and Project Representatives assisting the Architect. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, General Conditions (overall structure, Sections I-XI))

q: Under Sec. 25.02, at least how many days before the date of bidding must the Contractor ask the Architect to clarify which areas of work call for evaluating sub-contractor competency?
n: Sec. 25.02 requires the Contractor to seek this clarification at least fifteen (15) days prior to the bidding date, then submit a list of prospective sub-contractors for approval. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 25, Sec. 25.02)

q: Per Sec. 20.07(e), a claim for adjustment on questions of fact arising from a change order must be made within how many days from the date the change is ordered?
n: Sec. 20.07(e) requires claims for adjustment involving questions of fact to be asserted within fifteen (15) days from the date the change is ordered, unless the Architect extends this for proper cause. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.07(e))

q: Sec. 7.03(b) requires the Contractor to set benchmarks in at least how many places, spaced well apart?
n: Sec. 7.03(b) requires the Contractor to establish benchmarks in not less than two widely separated places, in addition to establishing benchmarks at each floor as work progresses. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 7, Sec. 7.03(b))

q: Which description fits the Project Representative as defined in the General Conditions?
n: Sec. 1.05 defines the Project Representative as the full-time Construction Inspector hired by the Owner, duly authorized in writing to assist the Architect and Engineer in supervision of the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.05)

q: Under Sec. 27(d), the Contractor may suspend or terminate the Contract (on 15 days' notice) if the Owner fails to pay a sum awarded in arbitration for more than how many days after the award?
n: Art. 27(d) allows the Contractor this right if the Owner fails to pay any sum within thirty (30) days after its award by arbitration. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 27(d))
scenario: Under a UAP Doc. 301 contract, a Contractor is reviewing whether recent events on its project give it grounds, under Art. 27, to suspend the work or terminate the Contract, each option carrying its own required written notice period.

q: The Architect has issued a Certificate of Completion. Unless the Contract names a different period, what is the longest the "Period of Making Good of Known Defects or Faults" may run from that Certificate's date, under Sec. 20.12?
n: Sec. 20.12 defines the Period of Making Good of Known Defects or Faults as not more than sixty (60) calendar days from the date of issue of the Certificate of Completion, unless the Contract expressly states otherwise. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.12)

q: For each manufactured equipment item, how many copies of complete catalog data does Sec. 9.02 require the Contractor to supply?
n: Sec. 9.02 (Equipment Approval Data) requires the Contractor to furnish three copies of complete catalog data for every manufactured item of equipment used in the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 9, Sec. 9.02)

q: Which UAP Doc. 301 term refers to the notice the Owner publishes, or the invitations sent to prospective bidders, that tell them the nature of the proposed project, the bidding date, and the estimated cost?
n: Sec. 1.15 defines the Advertisement or Invitation to Bid in these terms. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.15)

q: Sec. 30.01 requires the Contractor to assign someone on the work whose duty is to prevent accidents and damage to the Owner's property and adjoining property. Who is it, and to whom is the assignment reported?
o: A licensed safety officer, reported to the DOLE
The Contractor's Surety, reported to the Owner
A responsible member of the Contractor's organization, reported to the Architect
An insurance adjuster, reported to the Board of Arbitration
n: Sec. 30.01 requires the Contractor to designate a responsible member of his organization for accident/damage prevention and to report that person's name and position to the Architect. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 30, Sec. 30.01)

q: A typhoon, a recognized Act of God, delays the work on site. Under Sec. 21.04(a), the Contractor must file for a time extension within how many days from the occurrence of the delay?
n: Sec. 21.04(a) requires the Contractor to file the necessary request for extension within fifteen (15) days from the occurrence of the qualifying delay (e.g., Act of God, Owner-caused delay, strikes). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.04(a))
scenario: Under a UAP Doc. 301 building contract, the Contractor is handed a Notice to Proceed (NTP) dated March 1. From that date, the Contractor must keep track of several contract-administration deadlines set by Art. 21 (Time of Completion).

q: The Architect does not condemn or reject poor or inferior materials when they are delivered. Under Sec. 10.07(b), does that mean the Owner has accepted them?
o: No — defects found before final acceptance count
No — but only the Owner may reject
n: Sec. 10.07(b) provides that the Architect's failure to reject bad/inferior materials does not constitute acceptance if discovered before final acceptance of the work and release of the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 10, Sec. 10.07(b))

q: The General Conditions define the list of the parts of the work, each showing its value in materials and labor plus an allowance for profit and overhead, as the:
o: Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value
n: Sec. 1.24 defines the Breakdown of Work and Corresponding Value in these terms; it later becomes the basis for all Requests for Payment under Art. 22. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.24)

q: After Final Acceptance, the Owner releases the Performance and Payment Bonds on this project. Under Sec. 31.04, what Guarantee Bond must the Contractor provide, and for what period?
o: 15% of the price, for one year
30% of the price, for two years
10% of the price, for six months
30% of the price, for one year
n: Sec. 31.04 requires a Guarantee Bond of 30% of the Total Contract Cost (30% x Php 8,000,000 = Php 2,400,000), for a period of one year from the date of acceptance. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.04)
scenario: A Php 8,000,000 building contract under UAP Doc. 301 has been awarded to a Contractor. Before the Contract is signed, the Contractor must post the bonds that Art. 31 requires, and it must later replace those bonds in the order that Article sets out.

q: If no schedule or agreement sets when drawings will be supplied, Sec. 21.04(d) allows no delay claim for unfurnished drawings until how long after they are demanded?
n: Sec. 21.04(d) bars a delay claim for failure to furnish drawings until two weeks after demand for such drawings (and unless the claim is reasonable). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.04(d))

q: Unless the specifications say otherwise, Art. 13 requires manufactured articles to be applied, installed, connected, erected, used, cleaned, and conditioned according to:
n: Art. 13 (Manufacturer's Directions) requires compliance with manufacturer's printed directions unless the Specifications state otherwise. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 13)

q: Under Sec. 1.34, unless the Contract states otherwise, words like "approved," "directed," and "acceptable" mean approved, directed, or acceptable to which party?
n: Sec. 1.34 provides that such words mean approved/directed by or acceptable to the Architect, unless the Contract stipulates otherwise. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.34)

q: Before construction begins, Sec. 32.01 has the Owner provide a list of whom, so that they can be insured with matching coverage amounts?
n: Sec. 32.01 requires the Owner and Architect to give, prior to construction start, a list of project personnel needing insurance coverage, with the amount of coverage. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 32, Sec. 32.01)

q: Later the project reaches 55% completion, and a new Request for Payment is filed. Under Sec. 22.02, what retention applies to this and later billings?
o: 10% retention still applies to the full amount
No further retention is taken on the balance of the Contract, since 50% has been passed
Retention is doubled to make up for the earlier period
n: Sec. 22.02 provides that when 50% of the Contract has been accomplished, no further retention shall be made on the balance of the Contract. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.02)
scenario: Progress payments are being billed on a Php 10,000,000 building contract governed by UAP Doc. 301. For any given billing, the Contract's cumulative percentage of completion at that time decides which retention rules and payment procedures apply.

q: The Owner uses equipment on a temporary or trial basis before final completion and the Architect's written acceptance. Under Sec. 15.11, does this count as the Architect accepting the work?
o: No — trial use is not acceptance
Only if the Owner pays extra
n: Sec. 15.11 expressly states temporary or trial usage is not evidence of the Architect's acceptance of the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 15, Sec. 15.11)

q: A Contractor sees that the Drawings do not match actual site conditions but goes ahead without telling the Architect. Under Sec. 2.03(b), who carries the risk of that work?
o: The Owner and the Contractor equally
n: Sec. 2.03(b) provides that discrepancies must be immediately reported to the Architect/Engineer, and any work involving such discrepancies is done at the Contractor's risk. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 2, Sec. 2.03(b))

q: A question of fact is disputed under the Contract. Unless the Contract specifically says otherwise, whose decision on it is final and conclusive on the parties under Sec. 33.04(b)-(c)?
n: Sec. 33.04(b)-(c) makes the Architect's decision on questions of fact final and conclusive on the parties, except as otherwise specifically provided. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 33, Sec. 33.04(b)-(c))

q: Once the Architect approves a Request for Payment or issues a Certificate of Payment, the Owner must pay the certified amount within how many days under Sec. 22.07?
n: Sec. 22.07 requires the Owner to pay within fifteen (15) days from the date of approval of a Request for Payment or issuance of a Certificate of Payment. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.07)

q: Under Art. 17 (Protection of Adjacent Property and Existing Utilities), an existing utility is damaged through the Contractor's negligence or fault. Who pays for the repair?
o: The Owner and the Contractor equally
The Contractor, at his own expense
n: Sec. 17.02 (Existing Utilities) places the cost of repairing utilities damaged by the Contractor's negligence squarely on the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 17, Sec. 17.02)

q: Dimensions written on the Drawings disagree with measurements taken by scaling the drawing. What does Sec. 3.02 say?
o: The written figures are followed in preference to scaled measurements
The Contractor picks whichever is more convenient
The Architect must reissue the drawing every time
n: Sec. 3.02 (Coordination of Drawings and Specifications) provides that where figures are given, they govern over scaled measurements. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 3, Sec. 3.02)

q: According to Art. 34(a), the Architect represents the Owner during construction and may act for the Owner:
o: Only on design, never on money
Only as the Contract Documents or writing allow
Only when the Owner is abroad
n: Art. 34(a) limits the Architect's authority to act for the Owner to what is expressly provided in the Contract Documents or otherwise given in writing and shown to the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 34(a))

q: Before final payment, what Guarantee Bond does Sec. 22.11(g) require from the Contractor?
o: 30% of the Contract Price, covering one year after Final Acceptance
15% of the Contract Price, covering one year
30% of the Contract Price, covering two years
10% of the Contract Price, covering six months
n: Sec. 22.11(g) requires a Guarantee Bond equal to 30% of the Contract Price, covering a period of one year after Final Acceptance of the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 22, Sec. 22.11(g))

q: The Architect orders questioned work uncovered, and it turns out defective through the Contractor's fault. Under Sec. 20.03(b), who pays for the examination?
o: The Architect, out of his professional fee
n: Sec. 20.03(b) provides that if re-examined work is found not in accordance with the Contract Documents, the Contractor bears the cost. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.03(b))

q: Under Sec. 5.01, how many copies of shop or setting drawings, templates, patterns, and models must the Contractor submit, and who pays to prepare them?
o: Two copies, at the Contractor's own expense
Three copies, paid by the Owner
Four copies, at the Contractor's expense
One copy, paid by the Architect
n: Sec. 5.01 requires the Contractor to prepare, at his own expense, two copies of shop or setting drawings, templates, patterns and models for the Architect's review. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 5, Sec. 5.01)

q: Under Sec. 36.01, Project Representatives, Resident Architects, Resident Engineers, or Construction Inspectors assigned to a project are usually:
o: Recommended by the Architect, hired by the Owner
n: Sec. 36.01 describes these on-site technical personnel as recommended by the Architect and employed by the Owner, assisting in general supervision and direction of the work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 36, Sec. 36.01)

q: What right does the Owner keep for himself under Art. 23?
o: To let other, separate contracts connected with the work
To cut the Contract Price on his own
To hold back the Notice to Proceed indefinitely
To dismiss the Architect at will
n: Art. 23 (Sec. 23.01) reserves to the Owner the right to let other contracts in connection with the same work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 23, Sec. 23.01)

q: This time the Owner and the Contractor agree to price a change using unit prices already set in the Contract. Sec. 20.07(d)(2) allows this as long as the extra or credit does not exceed what percentage of the original contract value of that particular work?
n: Sec. 20.07(d)(2) allows valuation by stipulated unit prices provided the extra or credit does not exceed 25% of the original contract value of that particular work. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.07(d)(2))
scenario: A Php 20,000,000 lump-sum building contract under UAP Doc. 301 is in progress. Over the course of construction, a number of quantity and cost adjustments come up, and each is being checked against the General Conditions' rules on changes, extra work, and time extensions.

q: A Contractor skips the site visit before bidding and later asks for extra pay and more time because of site conditions it did not foresee. Is the claim valid under Sec. 6.02?
o: No — he should have visited before bidding
n: Sec. 6.02 (Site Conditions) places the burden on the Contractor to inspect the site before bidding; no extra compensation/extension is granted for the Contractor's own negligence. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 6, Sec. 6.02)

q: Which document is described as the printed documents setting out the procedural and administrative aspects of the contract — the very document this reviewer topic covers?
n: Sec. 1.19 defines the General Conditions themselves (UAP Doc. 301) as the printed documents stipulating the procedural and administrative aspects of the contract. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.19)

q: Under Sec. 26.02(c), a Sub-contractor's claims against the Contractor for extras, time extensions, or delay damages follow the same process as the Contractor's claims against the Owner, EXCEPT that the period for claiming extra cost is:
o: fifteen days, the same as the Contractor's
n: Sec. 26.02(c) shortens the Sub-contractor's claim period for extra cost to one week, unlike the Contractor's 15-day period under Sec. 20.08. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 26, Sec. 26.02(c))

q: The Contractor believes an instruction from the Architect will cost extra. Under Sec. 20.08, within how many days of receiving it must written notice go to the Architect, and by what point?
n: Sec. 20.08 requires written notice within 15 days after receipt of the instruction and, in any event, before proceeding to execute the work (except emergencies under Sec. 20.05). (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.08)

q: A deviation from the Drawings is discovered. Under Sec. 7.04(b), a licensed surveyor must certify it to the Architect within how many hours?
n: Sec. 7.04(b) requires the surveyor to certify any deviation from the Drawings to the Architect within 24 hours of its discovery. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 7, Sec. 7.04(b))

q: Which defined term covers anyone with a direct contract with the Contractor who acts for or on behalf of the Contractor in carrying out any part of the Contract — but not someone who only supplies materials without labor?
n: Sec. 1.07 defines the Sub-Contractor this way, expressly excluding a materials-only supplier. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.07)

q: Under Art. 28, before the Owner terminates the Contract for sufficient cause (such as the Contractor's insolvency or failure to pay sub-contractors), how many days' written notice must go to the Contractor and his Surety?
n: Art. 28 requires the Owner to give the Contractor (and Surety, if any) fifteen (15) days' written notice before terminating the Contract, upon the Architect's certification that sufficient cause exists. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 28)

q: Per Sec. 20.13, a known defect is found in an inspection just before the 60-day Period of Making Good ends. Within how many more days after that period ends must the Contractor still correct it?
n: Sec. 20.13 requires the Contractor to make good known defects within sixty days after issuance of the Certificate of Completion, or within fifteen days after the period's expiration if the defect was found by a pre-expiration inspection. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 20, Sec. 20.13)

q: Unless specified otherwise, how many material samples does Sec. 10.02(a) require for approval, and in what form does Sec. 10.02(d) require the request to be sent?
o: Two samples; letter of transmittal in duplicate
Three samples; letter of transmittal in triplicate
One sample; a verbal request is enough
Five samples; no transmittal letter needed
n: Sec. 10.02(a) requires three samples unless otherwise specified, and Sec. 10.02(d) requires a letter of transmittal in triplicate to accompany all sets of samples. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 10, Secs. 10.02(a) and (d))

q: Which term means additional information on the Contract Documents given to bidders before the date of bidding?
n: Sec. 1.16 defines the Bid Bulletin as additional information on Contract Documents issued to bidders before the bidding date. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.16)

q: Is the Owner liable, under Sec. 30.02, for death, disease, or injury to the Contractor's own employees or laborers, or for damage to the Contractor's plant or materials?
o: Only if the Owner was negligent
n: Sec. 30.02 disclaims Owner responsibility for injuries to the Contractor's own workforce and damage to the Contractor's plant/materials, placing that responsibility on the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 30, Sec. 30.02)

q: The Contractor expects to need Owner-furnished materials for a later phase of work. Under the proviso in Sec. 21.04(a), how many days before the materials are actually needed must it request them in writing, so it can later claim a valid time extension if the Owner fails to supply them?
n: The proviso to Sec. 21.04(a) requires a written request for Owner-furnished materials/information at least ten (10) days before they are actually needed, or no extension is granted for the Owner's alleged failure to furnish them. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.04(a))
scenario: Under a UAP Doc. 301 building contract, the Contractor is handed a Notice to Proceed (NTP) dated March 1. From that date, the Contractor must keep track of several contract-administration deadlines set by Art. 21 (Time of Completion).

q: Sec. 10.08 allows no time extension or substitution of materials for delays in imported materials, fixtures, appliances, and equipment when the delay is caused by:
o: a change ordered by the Architect
n: Sec. 10.08 provides no time extension or material substitution is allowed for delay due to the Contractor's own negligence or inadvertence in arranging for imported materials. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 10, Sec. 10.08)

q: Under Sec. 1.25, when is a "Written Notice" valid?
o: Delivered in person or by registered mail
n: Sec. 1.25 defines Written Notice as information delivered in person or sent by registered mail to the last known business address. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.25)

q: Under Sec. 31.04, how long after Final Acceptance of the work — and only once the Guarantee Bond is furnished — does the Owner release the Performance and Payment Bonds?
n: Sec. 31.04 provides that the Performance and Payment Bonds are released after the expiration of two (2) months from Final Acceptance of the work, and only after the Guarantee Bond has been furnished. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 31, Sec. 31.04)

q: How do the General Conditions classify the Contractor's payment for late completion under Sec. 21.05 (Liquidated Damages)?
o: As liquidated damages, not a penalty
As an advance on the final billing
As a forfeiture of the Performance Bond
n: Sec. 21.05 expressly states the payment is made as liquidated damages, and not by way of penalty, and may be deducted by the Owner from any sum due the Contractor. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 21, Sec. 21.05)

q: What does Sec. 14.02 forbid the Contractor to do to any part of the structure?
o: Load it beyond what is safe
n: Sec. 14.02 (Safeguard for Structure) prohibits the Contractor from loading or permitting the structure to be loaded with weight endangering its safety. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 14, Sec. 14.02)

q: As defined in Sec. 1.28, Local Laws include:
o: All laws and regulations that apply
n: Sec. 1.28 defines Local Laws broadly as all laws, ordinances, and governmental regulations applicable to the project. (Source: UAP Doc. 301, Art. 1, Sec. 1.28)
